title: The Yield Engine
subtitle: A case study of Axon, the engine behind AppLovin Ads
author: Michael Hoydich
illustrations: Generated with Codex (GPT image model), risograph style, fictional
thesis: Yield is prediction times feedstock. The engine is rented; the feedstock is yours.

public_figures.label: Daily active users on the network

yield_mechanisms: The deep-funnel purchase signal is the fuel
The three-screen ad unit is a funnel: video, interactive end card, product carousel
The engine is paid for prediction quality, not impression volume
Creative is the feedstock and it decays weekly
scale_ladder: Owned and mediated game inventory, targeted contextually
Pixel, conversions API and Shopify app for honest purchase values
Generators for end cards and video
Three buying contracts as the whole interface
doubts: Dashboard is click-only and conservative; third-party attribution is generous; geo holdouts can show no lift
Benchmark mean (1.7x Meta efficiency) and median (0.9x) disagree
Model improvement is not on a schedule; Q2 2026 grew 4% sequentially

field_note.category: hemp-derived THC seltzers and gummies, restricted, 21+, limited ship states

timeline.event: Axon account opened; $5,000 credit offered for $5,000 spent in 60 days
AppLovin launch playbook session; constant creative is the rule
Creative supply about five re-cut videos a week; team debates creative agency vs channel manager
Ten 9:16 boards generated in an evening; ten-ad handoff set with legal bar and human preflight
Month-to-month specialist engaged with spend ceiling, margin-true return threshold, dashboard as system of record

checklist: Yield = prediction x feedstock; budget against the second
Wire pixel plus server-side events with one dedupe id per paid order before the first dollar
Build a weekly creative supply chain: boards, cuts, captions, legal bar; five to seven concepts a week
Leave the account alone for seven days; scale 30-40% every two or three days after
Pick the system of record and a margin-true return threshold in writing
Run a geo holdout at the intended spend level
If restricted, design creative for review
boundary: No incrementality claim for Good Feels, no spend or revenue published, no agency endorsed. Figures marked reported are unverified by Industry Next.
